prompt: Walk an exception's cause chain: rootCause returns the deepest cause and chainNames lists every link as "Outer -> Inner". Both must survive a chain that loops back on itself.
explanation: getCause() exposes one link of a wrapped exception, so finding the real problem means following that link until it runs out. Because nothing stops a hand-built exception from naming itself (or another exception that names it back) as its cause, a naive while loop can spin forever; keeping a list of the exceptions already visited and comparing with == makes the walk safe. getClass().getSimpleName() gives the short type name used to render the chain.
hints: Both methods are the same walk: start at error and repeatedly move to current.getCause() until that is null.
Keep a List<Throwable> of links you have already visited and stop the loop when the next cause is one of them -- compare with == rather than equals.
Build the chain text with a StringBuilder, appending " -> " before every name except the first.
